paper.title_en: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
paper.abstract_en: We propose quantum sine imaginary-time evolution (QSITE), a quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of a Hamiltonian. QSITE approximates imaginary-time evolution through an exact sine filter. We give two circuit implementations of this operator: a sequential one that applies it as a concatenation of linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), reusing two ancilla qubits across steps via mid-circuit measurement, and a coherent one based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). A telescoping identity shows the two prepare the same state and succeed with identical probability, differing only in how that probability can be boosted. QSITE belongs to the family of ancilla-based probabilistic imaginary-time filters and we state rigorous convergence guarantees: we prove that the QSITE operator converges uniformly to the exact ITE operator, that the prepared state converges to the ideal ITE state, and that the filter probability increases monotonically with each concatenation step. Although the construction applies to an arbitrary Hamiltonian, we specialize it to optimization Hamiltonians, and this specialization is what exposes its structure more easily. Since MaxCut eigenvalues are integers, the probability of failure is periodic in the evolution time, yielding safe zones, the first located analytically and the second numerically. For MaxCut we further show that, when the tolerated energy error is a fixed fraction of the ground-state energy, the probability of failure can be bounded below 1/2 with concatenation steps growing linearly with the number of qubits in the first safe zone. We present numerical results for random Erdös-Rényi instances with up to 24 qubits and benchmark QSITE against QAOA.
